[b]LAMANDICAN TIMES HERALD[/b]

[b]Lamandican Man, 25, Arrested After Using Fireworks To Power Chariot, Then Crashing It Into A Mill [/b]

Oscar Altman Rathoma, was detained Sunday after using fireworks to propel himself in a chariot down Weptowner Asimc in the village of Las Vegas Del Sol in Mitremtion province, roughly 80 miles northwest of Mitremtion city. According to the Santa Eugenia County Constabulary, he did this to raise funds for the charity Chariots For Hire. According to reports, Rathoma climbed into a chariot with a few tons of fireworks attached to its back to power it forward. Fireworks were lit, and the chariot fired eastward down Weptowner Asimc. However, the chariot had no breaking device, meaning there was no way to stop it from its collision course with a textile mill at the end of the road. Rathoma in his chariot, careened into the mill, causing a partial collapse of the structure. Luckily, the mill was closed on that day and Rathoma was successfully treated for non-life threatening injuries at Mariam Hospital in nearby Sedgeville.

[b][u]The AIS-Corp. dilemma[/u][/b]

AIS-Corp. was delighted to have gained the Nordiheimian militaries attention and funding to create the FARV-40, as this would increase their portfolio in Nordiheims military market.
Infact some of the engineers had allready come up with a name for it, the Kakapo.

There was however a problem, while they had made the armored car AC-4B "Kiwi" and its different variants(including the initialy unintended ones) it had been some time since they last designed a propper vehicle for the military and the engineers that had done so had retired.
Obviously they had no trouble with the weapon system and the turret, that was the easy part of the vehicle, but the road part was more complicated for them as suspension and combustion engine was not their strongsuit.
Give them a problem to do with the engine of a missile or the complex system of a anti-air targeting algorytm and they would have no problem, it was their ting after all.

They did not realy want to cooperate this project with the 'Karlson Company' or 'Midarms' as they were direct competitors that would take such an opurtunety to point out all their flaws while keeping silent about their strenghts, and goind to one of the state owned companies would joust look silly as that could make it look like they should have joust done it themselfs.

One of the board members of the company then suggested a very interesting idea, why not hit up a cooperation with the Lavian company "Makinar Armor Workshop"(MAW/MAX) like it was done with the creation of the AFV-5G105 Cassowary, that company had loads of experience with vehicle suspensions and engines.
They could proberly even secure some funds or even future contracts with the [nation]Lavinsworth United Islands[/nation] goverment if they played their hand carefully wich made it a potentialy great opportunety for their company.
The company board did not take long to arrive on an agreement to do joust this, in adition to try and get both goverments in on it aswell.

Later that week the AIS-Corp. CEO would invite representatives from Makinar Armor Workshop together with people from the goverments of Nordiheim and Lavinsworth to a secure meeting to discuss such a project opportunety under the explanation that it would;
[i][u]"Evolve the project to someting far greater then what a singel company would be able to achive in a reasonable time to take advantage of it on the current battlefield and military market!"[/u][/i]
They gave the name for the future vehicle as "FARV- 40 Kakapo".
The meeting would also contain a full presentation on what they allready had for the project in curent teoretical and tested abilities aswell as what they expected that the cooperation could add to it.

[nation]Shahzada[/nation] RP[/quote]
The MAW company, one which has made many vehicles for Lavia and the export market, would accept this offer. While the company is majority owned by the government as it used to make most of the armored vehicles in Lavia, it must now compete with companies such as Ijesa Dynamics and NLPC. This proposal for a new scout vehicle would help them greatly, replacing their own joint design of the MAX-11 ARV. 

Bringing together it's wheeled vehicle engineers, it would begin forming up plans for such a vehicle before even being informed of the proposed design, trying to find the best hull just based on what has been talked about over communications before the meeting.
